elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 5(a) as rendered retains the fee floor: "(but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services)". The minimum commitment survives; it is only qualified by the new proviso.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Client remains obligated to pay a monthly floor irrespective of services actually requested, so payment is not limited to usage or ordered Services.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Inserted proviso: "The minimum monthly fees set forth in Section 5(a) apply only during the current 12-month term"; this overrides the Section 13 automatic successive one-year renewals carrying forward the same unconditional minimums and the open-ended Section 4/Section 14 lock-in.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted proviso: the minimums "may be reduced by Client upon 30 days' written notice" — correct party direction (Client, our side) and the stated 30-day notice period.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Inserted proviso: "any shortfall against such minimums will be trued up rather than charged as a penalty."

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: a single inserted proviso supplies all three atomic elements in operative language (12-month term limitation, Client-side 30 days' written notice reduction right, shortfall true-up in lieu of penalty), with no element left merely to the margin comment.

Preferred level is correctly not claimed: the fee floor in Section 5(a) is expressly retained, so Client still owes minimums irrespective of usage. The rationale acknowledges this trade-off (deleting the floor would require collateral edits to the Section 6 carve-outs), which is consistent with the redline guidance to narrow to the fallback with minimal edits.

Minimality holds: one concise sentence, no survival tails, expense language, extra damages categories, audit rights, or procedures beyond the three selected elements. Favourable existing language (Section 6's one-year price freeze and most-favoured-rate covenant; Section 13's domain-ownership retention) is untouched.

Intent preserved: invoicing cadence, 15-day payment terms, Exhibit A/B schedules, the Section 13 term/renewal mechanic and Section 14 termination mechanic all survive without contradiction; the proviso qualifies only the minimums and creates no dangling defined term.

Non-blocking notes for the drafter: (1) the insertion cites "Section 5(a)" while retained Section 6 twice refers to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" — that mismatch is pre-existing in the document, but the drafter may wish to conform the reference so the new proviso and Section 6 point to the same section. (2) Section 6 still bars Client from obtaining supporting documentation for, or contesting, the minimum monthly fees, which sits awkwardly beside a true-up mechanic; this is retained original language and not a fallback element, so it is a rationale note rather than a defect.
